rules.statement: A purchaser is not obligated to implement a contract where the vendor had no title at the time of sale, and the purchaser can avoid the contract if induced by fraud.
rules.supporting_quote: I do not think the question can be decided so simply. The cases cited by the learned District Judge refer to instances where vacant possession had been given. The defendant has averred in his answer that the plaintiff falsely and fraudulently represented to him that he had a good title to the land and that it was only after the execution of the deed that he discovered plaintiff had no title, and that the deed passed nothing at all. Can the defendant be precluded from proving this averment, and if he succeeds in proving it, will he be liable to pay the price ?
